query: Explain what leads a company to be based in one region rather than another.

per_column.name: industry_domain
per_column.rationale: Industry sector plausibly drives location choice (e.g., semiconductors near fabs, fintech near financial centers). This is a strong candidate cause of regional clustering and functions as a treatment/attributable driver.

per_column.name: talent_skill_requirement
per_column.rationale: Skill needs (specialized STEM vs general) both influence where a firm locates (near talent pools) and correlate with the industry/type of company. It is a plausible common cause of locational pull and the firm's characteristics, so it acts as a confounder for the location decision.

per_column.name: capital_proximity_indicator
per_column.rationale: Access to venture capital vs self-funded is a classic driver of regional location (firms locate near capital hubs). This is itself an attributable cause of the outcome rather than a common cause of another treatment.

per_column.name: company_maturity_signal
per_column.rationale: Company maturity/stage plausibly affects both funding structure/industry mix (treatment) and where a firm ends up located, making it a common cause worth adjusting for.

per_column.name: technology_innovation_posture
per_column.rationale: Innovation posture (cutting-edge research vs incremental) largely follows from industry and talent choices and in turn shapes location; it sits on the causal path rather than being a pre-treatment common cause, so it is more mediator than confounder.

per_column.name: target_market_vertical
per_column.rationale: Target market (enterprise B2B vs consumer) plausibly co-determines industry/funding and location preferences, acting as an upstream common cause.

judge.rationale: The query names no candidate causes or confounders, so all added columns are surfaced from the data rather than copied from the query. The system supplies plausible treatments (industry_domain, capital_proximity_indicator) that are attributable drivers of where a company is based, satisfying part (a). It also supplies several pre-treatment variables (talent_skill_requirement, company_maturity_signal, target_market_vertical) that plausibly act as common causes of both firm characteristics and location, satisfying part (b) with genuine, non-query-named confounders. Quality is moderate rather than high because the causal structure among these firm-attribute columns is loose (they are more correlates of firm type than clean common causes of a well-separated treatment/outcome pair), and technology_innovation_posture is better read as a mediator, which would bias attribution if adjusted for. Overall this is real causal reasoning surfacing non-obvious confounders, but with imperfect treatment/confounder separation.
